series_covered: all 12 (each series checked at 8-15 positions incl. x=0 and x~1)
method: Independent of the extractor's vector-path parsing: page 13 re-rendered with pymupdf at 1200 dpi (clip x 140-500 pt, y 15-180 pt); axes calibrated from raster gridline/spine pixel centres (subpixel, darkness-weighted) - not from the PDF drawing commands; curves read from dark-pixel runs (grey<100/255) per column (or per row on the steep Israeli segment), with local quadratic fits in (x, log10 H); overlapping curve pairs separated by resolved runs or by edge + half stroke thickness; values at x=0 (hidden under the left spine) by extrapolation from x=0.004-0.03. Style identity checked visually on zoomed 1200 dpi crops and on the provided 300 dpi render.

calibration_check.x: linear confirmed: London spine/gridlines at px 181.74, 670.59, 1159.45, 1648.38, 2137.21, 2626.15 (x=0..1 step 0.2), residual <0.07 px; Israeli 3115.00 ... 5559.46, residual <0.07 px. Same mapping as extractor (x_pt->x) to <1e-4.
calibration_check.y: log10 confirmed: 13 gridlines (4,5,7,8,9,10,30,50,60,70,80,90,100) fit px = -1252.079*log10(H) + 3187.331 with residuals <=0.3 px (one 1.2 px); spacing ratios match log10 (e.g. 4->5: 1249 px/dec, 9->10: 1245 px/dec), NOT linear. Bottom spine -> H=3.00, top spine -> H=201 (i.e. 200 within 0.5%). Extractor log10 map agrees with mine within 0.0006 decades (0.14%).
calibration_check.units: y = H_crit; the axis label carries no unit, metres inferred (Table 1 uses kN/m3 and kPa) - consistent with extractor's 'H_crit (m)'.

series_identification_check: Confirmed. Legend (and paper text p.12: 'solutions of Wu et al. ... solid lines ... dashed lines and dash-dotted lines refer respectively to the filtration velocity-based variational principle and pore pressure-based FE formulation'): dashed = K.v'_opt, solid = r_p=0.25 (Wu et al.), dash-dot = -grad u'_FE. Zoomed 1200 dpi crops show the extractor's dash-dot polylines run through the dash+dot strokes and the solid polylines through continuous strokes, including the overlapping beta=60 solid/dash-dot pairs (London x=0.4, 0.9; Israeli x=0.4, 0.9) and the dashed/dash-dot pairs near x=0.1. beta assignment (upper family = 30/35 deg, lower = 60 deg) matches the annotation arrows.

special_points.israeli_b35_offscale: Confirmed that Israeli b35 dashed and dash-dot start above the axis top: the straight (x, log10H) segment fitted from raster row runs (x 0.04-0.1) crosses H=200 at x=0.0085 (dashed) and 0.0079 (dash-dot) [extractor 0.0086 / 0.0077], gives H(0.1)=46.83 / 39.15 [46.83 / 39.24] and extrapolates to H(0)=229.0 / 230.2 [229.3 hidden]. The x=0 value is not printed in the figure; treat as off-scale (>200).
special_points.kinks: Israeli b35 seepage curves have a real kink at x=0.1 (visible in the raster); Israeli b35 r_p curve has a visible kink at x~0.125 - consistent with the extractor's polyline vertices.
special_points.x1_extrapolations: Flagged x=1 extrapolations agree with raster reads at x=0.98-0.99 (London dash-dot b60 5.45 vs 5.40 merged pair; Israeli dashed b35 8.608 vs 8.611; Israeli dashed b60 4.772 vs 4.774).

problems: Minor/cosmetic: 'first_visible_point' for the four solid curves at x=0 is 0.4-0.9% above the curve's own points[0] (London b30 95.62 vs 95.11; Israeli b35 140.26 vs 139.05; London b60 10.95 vs 10.90; Israeli b60 7.93 vs 7.89), apparently taken from the stroke outline edge, not the centreline. Within tolerance; points[0]/resampled[0] are the correct centreline values.

Not an error but a usage caveat: resampled[0] = 229.3 m for Israeli b35 dashed and dash-dot is off-scale (hidden by the axes clip); the extractor flags this correctly (starts_above_axis_top=true, first_visible_point at H=200).
Not verifiable from the printed figure: the hidden x=0 value 229.3 m; my extrapolation of the visible straight segment gives 229.0-230.2 m, consistent.
Unit 'm' is inferred, not printed on the axis.
